source_evidence.excerpt:
Let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank. Put
$A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$. Then $A_H$ is symmetric positive definite, hence
invertible, and the map $C=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$ of
[[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]] satisfies

$$C^2=C,\qquad CP=0,\qquad P^{\mathsf T}A_hC=0,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}A_h=A_hC.$$

Consequently $\operatorname{Ran}(C)=\operatorname{Ran}(P)^{\perp_{A_h}}$;
$C$ is the orthogonal projector onto that complement in the energy inner
product $\langle x,y\rangle_{A_h}:=x^{\mathsf T}A_hy$.

Let $A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank, where $1\le m\le n$. Put
$A_H=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP$. Then $A_H$ is symmetric positive definite, hence
invertible, and the map $C=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h$ of
[[def-galerkin-coarse-grid-correction]] satisfies

$$C^2=C,\qquad CP=0,\qquad P^{\mathsf T}A_hC=0,\qquad C^{\mathsf T}A_h=A_hC.$$

Consequently $\operatorname{Ran}(C)=\operatorname{Ran}(P)^{\perp_{A_h}}$;
$C$ is the orthogonal projector onto that complement in the energy inner
product $\langle x,y\rangle_{A_h}:=x^{\mathsf T}A_hy$.

Work over the real field with standard coordinate inner products. Let
$A_h\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite (equivalently,
positive definite in the Cholesky convention of
[[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]]) and let
$P\in\mathbb R^{n\times m}$ have full column rank, where $1\le m\le n$.
The map $P$ sends coarse-grid coordinate vectors to fine-grid coordinate
vectors; its Euclidean adjoint is the transpose $P^{\mathsf T}$ by
[[thm-matrix-of-the-adjoint-is-the-conjugate-transpose]]. Define the **Galerkin
coarse matrix**

$$A_H:=P^{\mathsf T}A_hP.$$

Whenever $A_H$ is invertible, define the **exact Galerkin coarse-correction
error map**

$$C:=I_n-PA_H^{-1}P^{\mathsf T}A_h.$$

This definition is conditional on invertibility of $A_H$. The next theorem
proves that condition from positive definiteness of $A_h$ and full column rank
of $P$. The formula is in exact real arithmetic; a rediscretized operator is
not identified with $A_H$ unless equality is separately shown.

Let $n\ge 1$ and $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$; over $\mathbb R$ the same definition uses transpose
instead of conjugate transpose.

The matrix $A$ is **Hermitian positive definite** if $A=A^*$ and

$$x^*Ax>0$$for every nonzero vector $x\in \mathbb C^n$. A **Cholesky factorisation with positive diagonal** of $A$ is a factorisation$$A=LL^*,$$

where $L$ is lower triangular and every diagonal entry of $L$ is a positive real
number.

The Hermitian terminology matches
[[def-sesquilinear-and-hermitian-forms-over-a-field-with-involution]], and the
triangular terminology matches
[[def-triangular-and-diagonal-matrices-over-a-commutative-ring]].

Let $F$ be a field, let $m,n,p\in\mathbb N$, and let
$A=(a_{ij})\in M_{m\times n}(F)$ and
$B=(b_{jk})\in M_{n\times p}(F)$. Their **matrix product** is the matrix
$AB\in M_{m\times p}(F)$ whose entries are

$$(AB)_{ik}:=\sum_{j\in n}a_{ij}b_{jk}.$$

The sum is the finite sum in the additive commutative monoid of $F$. If $n=0$,
it is the empty sum, so $AB$ is the zero matrix of shape $m$ by $p$.

The **identity matrix** $I_n\in M_n(F)$ has entry $1$ when $i=j$ and entry $0$
when $i\ne j$. In particular, $I_0$ is the unique empty matrix in $M_0(F)$.

Let $A\in M_n(\mathbb C)$ be Hermitian positive definite in the sense of
[[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]]. For vectors
$u,v\in\mathbb C^n$, define the **energy inner product**

$$\langle u,v\rangle_A:=\langle Au,v\rangle,$$

where $\langle \cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is the standard coordinate inner product of
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Because $A$ is Hermitian positive
definite, this is an inner product on $\mathbb C^n$, and its induced norm

$$\|u\|_A:=\sqrt{\langle u,u\rangle_A}$$

is the **energy norm** of $u$.

Equivalently, if $A=LL^*$ is the Cholesky factorization from
[[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]], then
$\langle u,v\rangle_A=\langle L^*u,L^*v\rangle$ and
$\|u\|_A=\|L^*u\|_2$.

empty_coarse_mathematics.calculation: For n>=1 and m=0, R^0={0}; the unique P:R^0->R^n has full column rank0 and range{0}. A_H=P^T A_h P is the unique0x0 matrix. The unique map R^0->R^0 is bijective and equals its own inverse/identity. With that explicit empty inverse convention, P A_H^{-1} P^T A_h is the n-by-n zero matrix by the already published empty-sum matrix-product convention. Hence C=I_n, C^2=C, CP=0, P^T A_h C=0 and C^T A_h=A_h C; Ran(C)=R^n=Ran(P)^{perp_A}.
empty_coarse_mathematics.important_limit: Under the present def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal domain, the0x0 matrix is not an instance of the defined SPD predicate. Its inverse cannot be justified by applying the positive-dimensional HPD unique-minimizer theorem. Thus simply deleting the new dimension clause without a separate convention/claim split would restore the genuine defect.
